title: Plover nests hatched with and without fencing
bodyMd: Ecologist Dagny Lorentzen monitored plover nests on four beaches. On each beach, some nests were surrounded by low wire fencing that keeps out foxes and gulls, and the rest were left unprotected. The table shows the percentage of nests in each group that hatched at least one chick.

data.caption: Percentage of unfenced and fenced plover nests that hatched at least one chick on four beaches (Lorentzen).

accessibilityText: A four-row table of plover nesting results. Columns are beach, the percentage of unfenced nests that hatched, and the percentage of fenced nests that hatched. Kestrel Point: 20 percent unfenced, 45 percent fenced. Ostby Sands: 40 percent unfenced, 70 percent fenced. Marren Cove: 30 percent unfenced, 57 percent fenced. Holm Bar: 50 percent unfenced, 72 percent fenced.

provenance.notes: Original data set written for this item bank. The ecologist, the beaches and every figure are invented. The numbers were chosen so that the beach with the largest gain in percentage points (Ostby Sands, 30 points) differs from the beach with the largest proportional gain (Kestrel Point, a factor of 2.25), and so that no other beach reaches a factor of 2.
